# Electrify

> A free electricity strategy game about running a utility: build power plants, balance supply and demand, and manage reliability, costs, and emissions.

## Start here

- [About the game](https://electrifygame.com/about.html): Background, sources, and contact.
- [Scenario directory](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios.html): Every official challenge and Legacy campaign chapter, with links to play.
- [How Electrify plays](https://electrifygame.com/power-grid-simulator.html): A guide for new players.
- [Classroom resources](https://electrifygame.com/classroom.html): Lesson plan and printable worksheet.

## Official scenarios

These pages describe playable simulations. Legacy chapters belong to one continuing campaign, and their play links open campaign setup.

- [Deep Freeze](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/deep-freeze.html): In Austin, you have four years to prepare for the February 2021 freeze. When residents turn up the heat, how much of your fleet will still be running?
- [Data Center Boom](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/data-center-boom.html): Manassas has six years to get ready for 100 MW of new data centers. They'll need power all night. What will you run after sunset?
- [Carbon Fee](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/carbon-fee.html): San Francisco's coal plant has years left in it, but you pay a fee on its emissions. How soon can you afford to replace it?
- [The Shale Boom](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/the-shale-boom.html): A shale gas boom is coming to Pittsburgh. The fuel discount will end long before a new gas plant wears out.
- [Paradise](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/paradise.html): Honolulu has plenty of sun and wind. On a calm night, you're paying for imported oil. There's no neighboring grid to buy power from.
- [Rise of Renewables](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/rise-of-renewables.html): Wind and solar are getting cheaper in California. Waiting could save you money, but new factories will need power before long.
- [Hurricane Season](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/hurricane-season.html): A hurricane is coming to Puerto Rico. Several plants can lose output at once, and the oil you'll need during repairs gets more expensive.
- [The End of an Era](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/the-end-of-an-era.html): Two coal plants power your Pittsburgh utility. They're getting older, and a replacement can take years to build. Your customers can switch suppliers sooner than that.
- [Heatwave + Drought](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/heatwave-and-drought.html): Spain's hottest days are hard on both sides of your grid. People turn up the air conditioning just as drought cuts hydro output and warm rivers limit reactor cooling.
- [Sudden Nuclear Shutdown](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/sudden-nuclear-shutdown.html): Your largest reactor supplies much of your Paris utility's power. Sometime during your five-year term it will shut down and stay offline.
- [Wildfire Emergency](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/wildfire-emergency.html): Wildfire will cut your Los Angeles utility's main power connection to a tenth of its usual capacity. What can you have ready by January 2025?
- [Load Shedding](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/load-shedding.html): Coal plants in your Johannesburg utility are breaking down faster than they can be repaired. Diesel can keep the lights on, if you can pay the fuel bill.
- [The River Runs Dry](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/the-river-runs-dry.html): Zambia's Copperbelt mines draw power around the clock. The reservoir on the Zambezi starts full, but an El Niño drought is coming.
- [Delhi Summer](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/delhi-summer.html): Delhi's air conditioners need more power each summer. In the heat of 2024, coal and gas plants will produce less, and a late monsoon will prolong the shortage risk.
- [Across the Valley](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/across-the-valley.html): Buy three neighboring utilities by December 2014. Once the deals close, their customers expect you to keep the lights on too.
- [Chernobyl: Recovery](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/chernobyl-recovery.html): In March 1986, all four Chernobyl reactors are producing electricity. A month from now, all four will be offline. Part of your job is paying for the cleanup.
- [First Light (1882–1901)](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/legacy-first-light.html): It's 1882. You own one small coal plant and sell electricity to 100 customers. Can you get their payments to cover the cost of keeping the plant running?
- [Beyond the Dynamo (1902–1921)](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/legacy-beyond-the-dynamo.html): More people want electricity from the company you started in First Light. How many new customers can the old plants serve before you have to borrow for another one?
- [Affordable Growth (1922–1941)](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/legacy-affordable-growth.html): Your California utility has more customers now. They need enough new capacity to meet rising demand, at a rate they can still afford.
- [Everybody Plugs In (1942–1961)](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/legacy-everybody-plugs-in.html): More California homes and businesses are plugging in. Halfway through your term you'll need spare power on top of what they're already using.
- [The Power You Don't Build (1962–1981)](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/legacy-the-power-you-dont-build.html): The oil shocks of the 1970s are coming. If your customers can use less electricity, your California utility can buy less fuel.
- [The Price of Power (1982–2001)](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/legacy-the-price-of-power.html): Regional power has helped supply your California utility. From July 2000, the northern connection won't be able to bring in as much.
- [The Sun Moves the Peak (2002–2021)](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/legacy-the-sun-moves-the-peak.html): Solar can cover a sunny California afternoon. This generation's goal is to serve 99.5% of evening demand, when solar output is falling.
- [Renew the Grid (2022–2041)](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/legacy-renew-the-grid.html): Which oil plants are still running after seven generations? It's 2022, and any you kept from 2000 or earlier will need to retire as California's demand grows.
- [A Different Kind of Growth (2042–2061)](https://electrifygame.com/scenarios/legacy-a-different-kind-of-growth.html): Your last twenty years come with one carbon budget. Every tonne your California utility emits in 2042 counts toward the same total as a tonne in 2061.
